programs.name: LA County Probation Pretrial Services
programs.summary: Probation's Pretrial Services gives judges background information and release recommendations, and staff work in most LA County courthouses. Programs it lists include Own Recognizance (OR) release, Electronic Monitoring and Drug Court. Note: the Pretrial Services Bauchet office closed Oct 1, 2025; call the Probation Information Center at (866) 931-2222.

programs.name: Community Collaborative Courts (CCC)
programs.summary: Treatment-based court for people charged with felonies or facing felony probation violations who have mental illness or substance use disorder, veterans, survivors of sex trafficking and at-risk young adults. If accepted, the person is placed on probation for 3-5 years with a treatment plan, and may earn a dismissal under PC 1203.4 on completion. Held at the Central, Van Nuys, Compton and Long Beach courthouses.

programs.name: Veterans Court
programs.summary: Alternative sentencing court for veterans charged with felonies or felony probation violations. It is run jointly by the Court, Public Defender, Alternate Public Defender, District Attorney, the VA and Public Counsel.

programs.name: Second Chance Women's Re-Entry Court
programs.summary: Alternative sentencing program for women, including mothers, who are charged with felonies and facing incarceration. It offers gender-responsive, trauma-informed treatment.

programs.name: Co-Occurring Disorders Court (CODC)
programs.summary: For people charged with felonies who have both mental illness and substance use disorder. Charges must be Prop 36-eligible (PC 1210) and/or non-violent.

programs.name: Sentenced Offender Drug Court (SODC)
programs.summary: Post-conviction substance use treatment program offered as an alternative to prison for felony clients with substance use disorder.

programs.name: Office of Diversion and Reentry (ODR) Permanent Supportive Housing
programs.summary: County diversion program, started in 2016, that connects eligible people in criminal cases to supportive housing. It is run jointly by the Superior Court's Criminal Division, the Public Defender, the Alternate Public Defender and the District Attorney.

programs.name: Community Outreach Court (COC)
programs.summary: Joint program of the LA City Attorney, LA County Public Defender, LA County Alternate Public Defender and the LA Mayor's Office of Community Safety.
programs.todo: Eligibility and locations are not described on the PD homepage; find the official COC page.

programs.name: Mental Health Diversion (Penal Code 1001.36)
programs.summary: California law (applies in LA) that lets a judge pause a misdemeanor or felony case for mental health treatment when a diagnosed mental disorder played a significant part in the offense. Diversion lasts up to 2 years for a felony or 1 year for a misdemeanor, and the charges are dismissed if it is completed successfully. Ask your attorney whether you qualify.
programs.todo: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov blocked automated loading (bot check) on 2026-10-10. Time limits were confirmed only from other CA courts' published guidelines. No LA-specific court page found; verify the statute text and LA procedure.

programs.name: Drug Pretrial Diversion (Penal Code 1000)
programs.summary: California law that allows pretrial diversion for certain drug possession offenses. If completed, the charges are dismissed. Ask your attorney whether you qualify.
programs.todo: Not verified on 2026-10-10 (leginfo bot check). Confirm program length and the eligible offenses, including any changes after Prop 36 (2024).

programs.name: Judge-Ordered Misdemeanor Diversion (Penal Code 1001.95)
programs.summary: California law that lets a judge offer diversion in many misdemeanor cases, with some offenses excluded. The charges are dismissed if the person completes the conditions. Ask your attorney whether you qualify.
programs.todo: Not verified on 2026-10-10 (leginfo bot check). Confirm the maximum period and the excluded offenses.

bail.note: Before paying a bail agent, check that their license is active using the California Department of Insurance License Status Inquiry (search by name or license number; see also https://www.insurance.ca.gov/license-status/). The court's felony, misdemeanor and infraction bail schedules are at https://www.lacourt.ca.gov/pages/lp/criminal/cp/bail-schedule. At the Clara Shortridge Foltz CJC, the Bail/Bond office is on the 5th Floor, Room 5-305, (213) 628-7700, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Phone numbers listed for jails are LASD's 24-hour facility lines. For custody status, call the LASD Inmate Information Line at (213) 473-6100. This is information only, not legal advice.
